questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 20 t on a road marked by this sign. There are three lanes in your direction. May you change lanes along path A to overtake the truck ahead?
options: Yes: the ban on the third lane applies only on motorways
Yes, if the truck ahead is travelling slower than 40 km/h
No: motorway rules apply on this road
Yes, but only in daylight and in good visibility
questions.explain: Sign 5.3 marks a road for motor vehicles. The requirements of Chapter 16 apply to it as to a motorway, including the ban on trucks heavier than 3.5 t going beyond the second lane. Path A leads into the third lane.

questions.q: Your heavily laden truck can travel no faster than 35 km/h. You will turn left at the next intersection. Which path should you follow?
options: Path A
Path B
Either of them
Neither: you may not leave the right lane
questions.explain: A vehicle travelling no faster than 40 km/h keeps to the far right lane, but changing lanes before a left turn is one of the exceptions. Before the turn you must move in advance to the far left position, so you change lanes along path A.

questions.q: Because of the length of your road train you cannot turn right from the far right lane, so you turn after moving to the adjacent lane on the left. A white car is going straight ahead in the right lane to your right. What should you do?
options: Turn: everyone gives way to a long vehicle at a turn
Let the white car pass and only then turn
Turn, switching on the hazard warning lights
Turn from the right lane, driving onto the pavement
questions.explain: You may move to the adjacent lane for a turn only if it is safe and does not impede other vehicles ⟦1⟧. The white car is going straight in the right lane and your turn crosses its path, so let it pass first. Driving onto the pavement is not allowed ⟦2⟧.

questions.q: You are in a truck about to change into the right lane. A white car is coming up behind you on the right and is barely visible in the mirror. What should you do?
options: Give way to the white car: it is going the same way without changing lanes
Change lanes: a switched-on direction indicator gives you priority
Change lanes: other vehicles give way to a large vehicle because of its size
Sound the horn and change lanes at once, before it catches up
questions.explain: When changing lanes you give way to vehicles travelling in the same direction without changing their course, and the white car is going straight along its lane. A direction indicator gives no priority ⟦3⟧. From a high cab a vehicle behind on the right is easy to lose sight of: check your mirrors and change lanes once it has passed.

questions.q: You are in a truck driving around an obstacle while a green car is changing lanes to the right at the same time. You both want to move into the middle lane. Who must give way?
options: You: a truck always gives way to a passenger car
Whoever switched on their direction indicator later
No one: both may change lanes at the same time
The green car: you are to its right
questions.explain: You and the green car are changing lanes at the same time, and you are to its right. In this case the driver who has another vehicle on their right must give way, that is, the green car. Size and the moment of switching on the indicator play no part here.

questions.q: The barrier is raised and no train is in sight. There are vehicles queuing beyond the crossing with about 8 m of free space there, and your road train is 18 m long. What should you do?
options: Drive on: the barrier is raised and there are no prohibiting signals
Drive on and wait on the tracks with the hazard warning lights on until the vehicles move away
Wait before the crossing until there is space for the whole road train beyond it
Drive on partly, so that only the trailer remains on the tracks
questions.explain: It is forbidden to enter a level crossing if there is a traffic jam beyond it that would force you to stop on the crossing, even when the barrier is raised. There are 8 m beyond the tracks and the road train needs 18 m: the trailer would remain on the tracks. Drive on only when the whole vehicle will fit beyond the crossing.

questions.q: You need to move a mobile crane across a level crossing, and because of a fault the boom will not fold into the transport position. What should you do?
options: Cross without stopping if the barrier is raised and no train is in sight
Cross slowly, at no more than 8 km/h, under the supervision of a duty officer
Cross only with the permission of the head of the railway track section
Cross the tracks away from the crossing, where there is no overhead contact wire
questions.explain: It is forbidden to move agricultural, road-building, construction and other machines and mechanisms that are not in the transport position across a level crossing without the permission of the head of the railway track section. Crossing the tracks away from a crossing is never allowed ⟦4⟧.

questions.q: What does this sign prohibit?
options: Trucks and tractors with trailers of any kind, and also towing
Any vehicles with a trailer, including passenger cars with a light trailer
Only road trains with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t
Only vehicles with a semi-trailer; a normal trailer is allowed
questions.explain: Sign 3.7 prohibits trucks and tractors with trailers of any type, including a semi-trailer, and also the towing of motor vehicles. It does not apply to a passenger car with a trailer. It applies in both directions.

questions.q: Your truck with a maximum authorised mass of 3 t is towing a trailer with a maximum authorised mass of 1.5 t. May you drive on past this sign?
options: Yes: the truck is lighter than 3.5 t, and the sign does not count the trailer
Yes, if the actual mass of the combination is currently less than 3.5 t
No: the authorised mass of the combination is 4.5 t, which is more than 3.5 t
Yes, but only in daylight and without overtaking
questions.explain: Sign 3.4 prohibits trucks and combinations with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t. For a combination, the authorised masses of the towing vehicle and the trailer are added together: 3 + 1.5 = 4.5 t. The actual load plays no part for this sign.

questions.q: Which truck with a maximum authorised mass of 10 t does this sign not prohibit?
options: A truck that is currently empty
A truck with its hazard warning lights on
A truck towing a trailer of no more than 750 kg
A truck with a diagonal white stripe on its sides
questions.explain: Sign 3.4 does not prohibit trucks with a diagonal white stripe on their sides and trucks designed for carrying people. An empty load body does not help: the sign looks at the maximum authorised mass, not the actual mass.

questions.q: Your truck with a maximum authorised mass of 11 t is, according to its documents, designed for carrying people: it has an enclosed body with seats for workers. May you drive past this sign?
options: No: the sign prohibits all trucks heavier than 3.5 t
Yes, but only if there are no people in the body at the moment
No, if more than 8 people are travelling in the body
Yes: the sign does not prohibit trucks designed for carrying people
questions.explain: Sign 3.4 prohibits trucks and combinations with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t, but it names the exceptions directly: trucks with a diagonal white stripe on their sides and trucks designed for carrying people. Your truck is exactly that kind.

questions.q: On an advance direction sign before an intersection there is sign 3.11 “Weight limit” with the figure 10 t and an arrow pointing sideways. You are driving a laden truck with an actual mass of 18 t. What does this direction sign mean?
options: Ahead is a section you may not enter, and the arrow shows the detour
Trucks heavier than 10 t may not turn in the direction of the arrow
In 10 km along the arrow there will be a weight check point
Along the arrow there is a parking area for trucks up to 10 t
questions.explain: Sign 5.20.1, the advance direction sign, is also used to show a detour around a section where one of signs 3.11-3.15 is placed. With an actual mass of 18 t you may not enter a section with sign 3.11 “10 t”, so follow the detour arrow.

questions.q: The actual mass of your road train is 28 t, but it is spread over five axles, and the most heavily loaded axle carries 5.8 t. May you drive on past this sign?
options: Yes: no axle carries more than 6 t
No: the total mass of the road train is far more than 6 t
No: sign 3.12 prohibits any road trains
Yes, but only if you uncouple the trailer and haul it separately
questions.explain: Sign 3.12 prohibits vehicles whose actual load on any axle is greater than the figure on the sign. The total mass does not matter for this sign: your heaviest axle load is 5.8 t, which is no more than 6 t.

questions.q: Your truck is 9 m long, and pipes in the body project 1.5 m beyond the tailgate. May you drive on past this sign?
options: Yes: the truck itself is 9 m long, and the projecting load is not counted
No: with the pipes the length is 10.5 m, which is more than 10 m on the sign
Yes, if the projection is marked with the “Oversized load” sign
Yes, if you drive slowly and switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explain: Sign 3.15 counts the overall length of the vehicle or combination together with the load: 9 + 1.5 = 10.5 m, which is more than 10 m. A projection at the rear of more than 1 m must be marked with the “Oversized load” sign ⟦5⟧, but this does not allow you to drive past this sign.

questions.q: Before a bridge there is sign 3.16 “50 m” with plate 7.4.1, as in the diagram. You are in a truck, and a passenger car is ahead of you. How must you drive?
options: Keep at least 50 m behind the passenger car
Keep 50 m only behind trucks; behind passenger cars a shorter distance is allowed
Drive no faster than 50 km/h to the end of the zone of the sign
No special way: the plate refers to the vehicle travelling ahead
questions.explain: Plate 7.4.1 extends the action of sign 3.16 to trucks, that is, to you. The sign prohibits driving closer than the stated distance to the vehicle ahead, whatever it is, so keep at least 50 m behind the passenger car.

questions.q: You are in a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 16 t and have passed sign 3.22, and then an intersection, as in the diagram. There were no other signs. A truck ahead is travelling at about 60 km/h, and the oncoming lane is clear. May you overtake it?
options: No: the prohibition of sign 3.22 applies until sign 3.23
Yes: the zone of sign 3.22 ended at the intersection
No: the truck ahead is travelling faster than 30 km/h
Yes, but only if the truck ahead moves over to the shoulder
questions.explain: The zone of sign 3.22 runs from where it is placed to the nearest intersection beyond it. You have already passed the intersection and there are no other prohibitions, so overtaking is allowed if it is safe ⟦6⟧. Signs 3.23 or 3.31 can end the zone before the intersection.

questions.q: You are in a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 16 t and have passed sign 3.22. The intersection is still ahead, as in the diagram. A truck ahead is travelling at about 60 km/h, and the oncoming lane is clear. May you overtake it?
options: No: until the nearest intersection you are in the zone of sign 3.22
Yes: the oncoming lane is clear and the marking is broken
Yes, if you finish overtaking before the intersection
Yes: sign 3.22 prohibits only the overtaking of passenger cars
questions.explain: The zone of sign 3.22 extends to the nearest intersection, and you have not reached it yet. The truck ahead is travelling faster than 30 km/h, so the exception for single slow-moving vehicles does not apply here.

questions.q: In a built-up area you are in a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 16 t and have passed sign 3.22. There are no more intersections, and no signs 3.23 or 3.31 either. Up to what point does the overtaking ban apply to you?
options: To the nearest exit from an adjacent area
To the end of the built-up area
To sign 3.21 “End of no-overtaking zone”
For 500 m from where the sign is placed
questions.explain: The zone of sign 3.22 runs to the nearest intersection beyond it, and in a built-up area without intersections, to the end of the built-up area. Signs 3.23, 3.31 or plate 7.2.1 can end it earlier. An exit from an adjacent area does not count as an intersection, and sign 3.21 ends the zone of sign 3.20.

questions.q: You are driving a goods van with a maximum authorised mass of 3 t, without a trailer. May you drive past this sign with no figures?
options: No: the sign prohibits all trucks, whatever their mass
Yes, but only if the van is empty and not carrying anything
Yes: with no figures it applies to trucks heavier than 3.5 t
No: the sign applies to any vans that are carrying a load
questions.explain: If sign 3.4 shows no mass, it prohibits trucks and combinations with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t. Your van is 3 t, so you may drive on. With a trailer, the sum of the authorised masses would be counted.

questions.q: You are in a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 10 t approaching a street with this sign. May you enter it?
options: Yes: the sign allows all motor cars except tractors
No, unless you are serving an enterprise or residents of the zone
Yes, if the actual mass of the vehicle with its load is less than 3.5 t
No, under no circumstances, even to unload in this zone
questions.explain: Sign 4.4 allows only passenger cars, buses, motorcycles, route vehicles and trucks with a maximum authorised mass of up to 3.5 t. Other vehicles may enter if they serve enterprises or citizens in this zone, via the intersection nearest to their destination.

questions.q: You are carrying acid, a class 8 dangerous good, and your vehicle displays “Dangerous goods” signs. May you drive past this sign?
options: No: the sign prohibits all vehicles with “Dangerous goods” signs
Yes, but only if you switch on the amber beacon
Yes: this sign does not apply to class 8 goods
No: the sign prohibits all trucks heavier than 3.5 t
questions.explain: Sign 3.33 prohibits vehicles with “Dangerous goods” signs that are intended for explosive and flammable goods of classes 1, 2.2-2.4, 3.1, 3.2 and 5.2. Class 8 is not on this list. Another sign, 3.32, prohibits all vehicles with “Dangerous goods” signs.

questions.q: What do signs 5.30.1-5.30.5 “Direction of travel for trucks” mean?
options: The recommended direction for trucks if one of the directions is prohibited to them
The direction of travel at the nearest intersection that is mandatory for all vehicles heavier than 3.5 t
The lane in which trucks are allowed to overtake on a motorway
A place where trucks are allowed to park for a rest or overnight stay
questions.explain: Signs 5.30.1-5.30.5 show the recommended direction for trucks, tractors and self-propelled machines if at an intersection their movement in one of the directions is prohibited. This is a hint for a detour, and the prohibition itself is introduced by other signs, for example 3.4.

questions.q: You were driving in the zone of sign 3.22 in a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 16 t and have passed this sign. There were no intersections. May you now overtake a truck travelling at about 60 km/h if the oncoming lane is clear?
options: No: the prohibition of sign 3.22 is cancelled only by sign 3.23
No: the prohibition applies up to the nearest intersection
Yes, but only if the truck is travelling slower than 30 km/h
Yes: this sign also cancels the prohibition of sign 3.22
questions.explain: Sign 3.31 “End of all restrictions” cancels several signs at once, including 3.16, 3.20, 3.22 and 3.24. After it the overtaking ban for trucks no longer applies. Overtake if the conditions of para. 77 are met.

questions.q: You are driving a road train 19 m long in an organised convoy on a road outside built-up areas with one lane in each direction. Must you keep a gap ahead so that overtaking vehicles can move in ahead of you?
options: No: this requirement does not apply in an organised convoy
Yes: on such a road it is mandatory for all combinations longer than 7 m
Yes, but only in hours of darkness and in poor visibility
No: it applies only to vehicles longer than 20 m
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas on two-lane roads, vehicles longer than 7 m and those subject to a speed limit keep a gap for overtaking vehicles. But the requirement does not apply if the driver is preparing to overtake, in heavy traffic and when driving in an organised convoy.

questions.q: Your truck, 6 m long, is carrying an overweight load, and a “Speed limit” identification sign with the figure 40 is fitted at the rear. It is a road outside built-up areas with one lane in each direction, and traffic is light. What distance must you keep to the vehicle ahead?
options: Any safe distance: the requirement applies only to vehicles longer than 7 m
At least 40 m, according to the figure on the “Speed limit” sign
One that lets overtaking vehicles move in ahead of you
As little as possible, so that those behind can see there is a jam ahead
questions.explain: A gap for overtaking vehicles is kept not only by vehicles longer than 7 m but also by vehicles subject to a speed limit. The speed of your vehicle is limited by the identification sign ⟦7⟧ and by the conditions for carrying an overweight load ⟦8⟧, so on a two-lane road outside built-up areas leave room ahead of you for an overtaking vehicle.
